title: fix(ui): the setup-pick sweep runs every frame, whatever the dock shows
body:
**Stacked on #666** (#664, setup picks disarm on page change). Review only this PR's own commit, `75c8b710`.

**P2 (#667, found in M5's review of #666):** #666's disarm sweep ran inside `pages::properties`, so only while the Properties tab was drawn. With the tab closed or hidden behind another tab, an armed Setups pick stayed armed and viewport clicks fed the hidden draft.

## What changed
- **`shell_layout`** wraps the dock with the sweep, once per frame.
  - **Before the dock:** if `layout::is_shown(dock, Properties)` is false, `axis_pick::disarm_all` runs. `is_shown` is new: the tab is in the dock, active in its leaf, and the leaf isn't collapsed.
  - **After the dock:** `axis_pick::disarm_hidden` runs.
- **Ordering:** viewport clicks are routed inside the dock, and egui_dock draws leaves by node index, so the viewport can draw before Properties.
  - The before-dock check closes the one-frame gap: a pane hidden by a click in frame N-1 is disarmed before frame N's viewport runs.
  - It also stops a stale `axis_rows_shown` from letting `hint_stray` swallow clicks while the pane is closed.
  - This is documented at the call site and in `docs/decisions/667-sweep-every-frame.md`.
- **`pages::properties`** loses #666's wrapper and is back to a single function. The rows still mark themselves.

## How tested
- **`setup_picks_disarm`, now 5 tests (headless, real clicks through the View door):**
  - `an_axis_pick_disarms_when_the_properties_tab_is_closed`: arm +Y by Edge and pick, close Properties, click the part, and the draft is unchanged. Reopening shows "Pick +Y edge" with the edge kept.
  - `a_plane_pick_disarms_when_another_tab_hides_the_properties_pane`: opening Machines in front of Properties disarms the face pick. Closing Machines shows "Pick a face" with the face kept.
  - Both fail without the fix. #666's three tests still pass.
- **Gate:**
  - ui lib 391 pass. The 1 failure is the known no-GPU `headless_run_succeeds` in the agent sandbox;
  - boundary_picks, edge_loop_pick and operations pass;
  - clippy is clean. No snapshot PNGs changed.

title: feat(post): Doosan DNM + Fanuc post processor (#614)
body:
(fork synced at v0.16.0)

Implements a dedicated post-processor dialect for Doosan DNM vertical machining centers with Fanuc 0i / 31i-M controls (#614).

## What changed

- **`assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`**:
  - Clean-room implementation specced from published Fanuc 0i/31i operator manuals and Doosan Infracore / DN Solutions DNM series programming guides (behavior only, clean-room protocol).
  - **Through-Spindle Coolant (TSC):** Supports `PARAM Coolant through-tool`. Emits Doosan high-pressure TSC M-code `M88` (with `M89`/`M09` on shut-off). Supports `useM8ForTSC` option for machines where TSC is triggered via `M08`.
  - **Rotary Table Brake (4th-axis A):** On index positioning (`G00 A...`), unclamps the pneumatic brake (`M11`) before rotating, and clamps the brake (`M10`) after positioning before cutting moves.
  - **High-Speed Smoothing / AICC (`G05.1 Q1` / `G05.1 Q0`):** Modal Fanuc AI Contour Control lookahead smoothing. Automatically deactivated (`G05.1 Q0`) prior to canned drilling cycles (`G73`, `G81-G89`), probing (`G31`), tool change, and program close, and reactivated on subsequent cutting moves.
  - **Chip Conveyor:** Commands `M31` (start) and `M33` (stop) when chip conveyor option is enabled.
  - **Probing:** Supports standard Fanuc `G31` macro-B skip moves and Renishaw Inspection Plus macro format (`G65 P9810`/`G65 P9811`) when `probingStyle: "inspection-plus"` is requested.
- **`assets/machines/doosan-dnm.mch`**:
  - Doosan DNM 5700 machine definition (X: 1020 mm, Y: 570 mm, Z: 510 mm, 12,000 RPM, rapid 36/36/30 m/min, coolants Flood M8, Mist M7, Through-tool M88).
- **Registry & Conformance**:
  - Registered in `BUILTINS` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs`.
  - Registered in `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs` (`POSTS` and `EXTENSIONS`), with all 13 golden `.nc` outputs locked under `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/doosan-dnm/`.
- **Decision Record**:
  - Recorded in `docs/decisions/614-doosan-dnm-post.md`.

## How tested

- **`crates/app/tests/doosan_dnm_post.rs`** (6/6 passing):
  - `doosan_dnm_posts_basic_milling_clean`: basic program structure, preamble, tool change, work offset, retracts, safe end.
  - `doosan_dnm_through_spindle_coolant_modes`: verifies M88/M89 default TSC and M8 option.
  - `doosan_dnm_rotary_brake_clamp_unclamp`: verifies M11 unclamp precedes A-axis indexing and M10 clamp precedes cutting.
  - `doosan_dnm_high_speed_smoothing_aicc`: verifies G05.1 Q1 engagement and G05.1 Q0 deactivation before canned drilling cycles.
  - `doosan_dnm_chip_conveyor`: verifies M31 start and M33 stop.
  - `doosan_dnm_probing_modes`: verifies standard G31 skip and Inspection Plus G65 macro formats.
- **`crates/app/tests/conformance.rs`** (6/6 passing):
  - `every_builtin_posts_every_golden_byte_exact` across all 13 goldens.
  - `every_builtin_registry_entry_compiles`, `every_builtin_declares_its_controls_file_extension`, `the_dialects_actually_differ`.
- Clippy `-D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- Physical cutting on a physical machine tool (the issue author `@spikeypineapple` offered to test on their DNM).

Changelog: Doosan DNM + Fanuc post processor with through-spindle coolant, 4th-axis rotary brake clamp/unclamp, G05.1 AICC smoothing, chip conveyor, and probing (#614)

body:

title: feat(setups): part alignment turns about the WCS origin and lays the picked face down
body:
**Stacked on #603** (#330, the face-lay rows, which also carries #593 and #573). Review only this PR's own commit, `e14ee4a2`.

#606 left three items to decide. Each is recorded in `docs/decisions/606-align-pivot.md`, with what was considered and dropped.

## 1. The typed-angle Apply turns about the WCS origin, with a choice
- **Default pivot: the setup's WCS origin.** That is the WCS entity's position, or zero if none is placed, read the same way as `posting::wcs_context`. The part point on the origin stays on it, which answers the maintainer's report that alignment "shifts the model relative to the origin".
- **Angles stay absolute from "as modelled".** Re-applying the same angles is refused ("already holds the part that way") rather than drifting. All-zero means "as modelled".
- **The choice:** an `about [WCS origin | part centre]` combo sits beside Apply, and the tooltip names the pivot. "Part centre" is the old behaviour.
- **Presets (Flip over X, Turn Z 90, …) still turn about the part centre,** and their tooltip says so. About the origin, a flip would put a part sitting on Z 0 under the table.
- **Code:** new `crates/app/src/setup_turn.rs` and `AlignPartToSetup::turn(…, pivot)`. `CommandKind::AlignPart` gains `pivot`. It is still **one undoable command**.

## 2. Lay on a plane defaults to face down (maintainer's call: recommended option taken)
- The face row's "Flip" becomes **"Face down"**, on for a new pick: the picked face sits on the plane with the part on top. The points row's "Flip points" becomes **"Points down"**, also on by default.
- **Only the UI draft default changed.** `PlaneLay::flip` keeps its meaning for the app, MCP and scripts.
- **Saved setups store the resulting transform, so old projects load and post identically.**

## 3. The structural test checks the pane, not the window
- `setup_page_alignment_rows_structure` now asserts every alignment control, including the new combo and Apply, lies inside the **properties pane's tab rect**.
- Putting the face row back on one line (the #330 regression) **fails** the test: `"Face down" … [[1349.8 344] - [1429.4 362]]` against the pane's right edge at x 1264.

title: refactor(sim): a carried field reads back as the column body, the same on both engines
body:
## What changed

**Stacked on #651** (#637 step C), which is stacked on #649 and #646. Merge them in order #646, #649, #651, then this. This is **#637 step D**.

**New `CarriedField::column_body(lattice, judged_before) -> Body`** (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field_body.rs`) reads the carried, clipped field onto the next setup's lattice (`Lattice { x0, y0, cell, nx, ny }`, new frame).
- **Per column:**
  - the **top** is one down-march (`march`);
  - the **floor** is step B's exact shell floor (`floor_at`);
  - a **flip** swaps them, since the new top is the old floor;
  - the **clip** trims the column, and `Clip::Empty` leaves every column empty;
  - a floor a cut reached, or a column the field cannot read, is **refused by name**.
- **The result** is the same `carry::Body` the column engine makes (new `Body::from_parts`), so `deviate` (the two-sided verdict), `display`, `volume` and `bounds` run **unchanged** on either engine.
- **Plumbing:** `march::world` is now `pub(crate)`.

**A decision, recorded in `docs/decisions/637-carried-field-read-back.md`:** this replaces the planned `Body = Column | Field` enum. The enum needed a second, field-native implementation of every `Body` method, each new verdict code to prove. The read-back reuses the one verdict the column carry already proves, and tops and floors still come from the field, never interpolated.

## How tested

- **New `crates/sim/tests/carry_engine_agreement.rs`, 2/2, about 3 s in debug.** The same 20×12 block, cut by the same slot (shallow at z 3, deep at z 1), is carried through **all 8 lattice turns** (quarter turns and flips) on **both** engines.
  - Per column, `empty_at` matches and the top and floor agree to **1e-6**.
  - The volumes agree to 1e-6, and `floor_judged` matches.
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`:** the sim suites pass. Named: field_carry 8, field_floor 3, stock_backend_parity 13, stock_columns 3, and app setup_carry 9, carried_verify 8, rest_across_setups 7.
- **Clippy** on sim and app with `-D warnings`: clean. No golden changed.

## Not exercised

- **Step E:** the app holders (#586) taking a field carry. Nothing in the app calls `column_body` yet.
- **A field-native verdict finer than the lattice:** possible later behind the same `Body` API.
- **The two #651 nits** (a `Display` for `ClipRefusal`, and the mod sort order) are left for step E, which touches the same file.

title: fix(turning): lathe tool orientation numbers read in the machine's turret frame
body:
**Stacked on #644**, which is stacked on #640. Review only this PR's own commit, `0f94a534`.

**P1 (#650):** #640 reads LinuxCNC's 1-9 orientation chart in the **front-turret** frame. Tormach PathPilot, a rear tool with X+ toward the tool, numbers the same physical tools mirrored in X: 1↔4, 2↔3, 6↔8, with 5, 7 and 9 unchanged. A PathPilot user entering their tool table's 3 would get the boring-bar tip.

## Evidence
These are the contributor's PathPilot Hub 8L v2.14.4 conversational samples, used as behaviour reference only.
- **(a) Facing with orientation 3 to centre:** fits only the mirror (rear 3 = front 2, tip (−X, −Z)).
- **(b) External thread wants 8:** fits only the mirror (rear 8 = front 6, tip at the axis).
- **(c) A chamfer refusing 3 with [1,5,6] / [2,6,7]:** fits the mirror only if PathPilot treated that chamfer as **internal**. Unmirrored, those are the OD chamfer sets.
  - Not forced. **Recorded and open:** one Hub check of an explicit OD chamfer with tool 3. If PathPilot still refuses it, the reading must be revisited before #626 relies on it.

## What changed
- **Machine key `general.turret`,** `front` or `rear`:
  - absent means front, and any other word is refused by name;
  - an editor field and the validator;
  - the built-in Lathe states `front`.
  - No Tormach lathe `.mch` exists yet, so none is marked rear.
- **Tools store the front-frame (canonical) code, the physical tool;** each machine **shows** its own number. A tool keeps its physical meaning across machines, and front projects and all front goldens are byte-identical.
- **`crates/tools/src/turret.rs`** handles the renumbering, the fitting lists, labels and captions.
- **Where the frame applies:** the post uses the op's own setup's machine.
  - The refusals, the defaults (OD 2 front / 3 rear; boring bar 3 / 2; blade left corner 2 / 3; blade codes [1,2,6] / [3,4,8]), the editor row and the `ORIENTATION q` note all use that machine's numbers.
  - Refusals are tagged "(front|rear turret numbering)".
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/650-turret-side.md`. It supersedes #640's line that the number doesn't depend on the turret side.

## How tested
- **New `lathe_turret_side` (7):**
  - rear 3 posts exactly front 2's path, and the rear default matches;
  - a rear facing with 3 reaches centre, pinned by a new golden `facing_rear.nc` (identical to `facing.nc` except for the note's number);
  - rear 8 posts (−r, 0), and rear 6 is refused with rear numbers;
  - each machine's refusal lists use its own numbers;
  - the chamfer data point under the mirror reading;
  - the `.mch` key parse and refusal;
  - a rear project round-trips byte-identical.
- **Also new:** `lathe_blade_corner::a_rear_turret_numbers_the_corners_in_its_own_frame`, tools `turret` units (4), and the ui orientation row's rear frame.
- **Gate:**
  - all 46 app binaries pass: lathe_*, turning_*, machine*, tool_*, tormach_*, project_roundtrip, commands_undo, conformance, golden_cl, posting;
  - tools lib 39 and post 55 pass;
  - clippy is clean on 4 crates.

title: fix(app): the lathe stroke check judges the posted radius, not world X
body:
**Stacked on #640** (#630, control-point posting and the built-in Lathe's X floor of -2.5). Review only this PR's own commit, `dd45a6c4`.

**P1 (#647):** the machine travel check compared each move's **world X** with a lathe's X band. Turning kernels carry their radius on the **Y meridian**, so a lathe radial over-travel was never judged. It also judged the nose-centre cache, not the control point the post writes.

## What changed
- **New `crates/app/src/machine/lathe_stroke.rs`.** On lathe-kind machines only, each op is judged on **`posting::nose::posted_path`**, the exact stream the post gets: the control point for the nose-centre turning ops, and the cache for the others.
  - **X** is the signed offset from the axis on the path's meridian, read as `fanuc-lathe.cps` `radiusOf` reads it, with the same 0.0005 tolerance. Past centre is negative and meets the floor.
  - **Z** is relative to the origin.
  - **Arcs** about the spindle axis are judged on their radius, with arc quarter points included.
  - **Any point off every meridian** is judged three ways: on signed world X, on its radius, and on Y against any Y band. No single reading can clear it.
  - **Refusal wording** is unchanged: "<op>: move i reaches v in X, the stroke is lo..hi".
  - **When the post refuses the orientation**, the check falls back to the nose-centre cache, so the op is still judged.
- **`machine/mod.rs` (+9 lines):** calls the lathe judge first and skips the world-X block for lathe machines. Mill and mill-turn checks are unchanged.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/647-lathe-stroke-radius.md`.

## How tested (`lathe_stroke`, now 10 tests)
- **New:**
  - `a_facing_control_point_below_the_x_floor_is_refused_by_name`: with the floor at -0.5, Face1 on the Y meridian is refused with "reaches -0.800 in X". It fails without the fix.
  - `a_turning_pass_beyond_the_x_ceiling_is_refused_by_name`: X max 9 on an r10 bar refuses Rough1. It fails without the fix.
  - `a_facing_control_point_on_the_x_floor_passes`: a guard at the band edge.

- **Updated:** `a_clearance_past_the_lathe_carriage_still_refuses_by_name` now expects Rough1 at Z 634.200, the control point (r 0.8 below the nose centre), not 635.000. Mill-turn still expects 635.000.

title: fix(turning): lathe posts write the tool's control point for its orientation, not the nose centre
body:
**P0 (#630):** lathe posts wrote the insert's **nose-centre** path under G40. With normal touch-off, the controlled point is the imaginary tip (LinuxCNC Lathe User Information §7.1), so turned diameters came out **2r oversize** and faces **r long**. Confirmed against the control vendor's own behaviour: PathPilot's conversational posts the orientation's control point with G40, and refuses a tool whose orientation can't make the cut. That sample is used as behaviour reference only.

## What changed
- **Tool orientation** (LinuxCNC 1-9 chart: Lathe User Information §3 figure, §7.1, §4.1):
  - `Tool.orientation: Option<u8>`. Turning inserts default to **2** (OD, cutting toward the chuck), boring bars to **3**.
  - Editable in the tool editor, which shows the default, through the undoable `ChangeTool`.
  - The project key is written only when set, so old files load with the default. 1-9 is enforced at command creation and at file read.
  - Fanuc's tip chart is different, and no post writes either number, so only the LinuxCNC chart is modelled.
- **One shared conversion,** `crates/post/src/post/nose_tip.rs::control_point_path`, called once from `posting::op_streams` (`posting_nose.rs`), not per .cps:
  - Every move, rapids and arc centres included, shifts by r·(ox, oz) for the orientation.
  - This is exact on diameters, faces, tapers and arcs: the cutting path is already the profile offset by r, and the insert is rigid.
  - Refused by name: a path on two meridians or off every meridian, a C angle, an off-plane arc, and paths carrying cycle, thread, compensation or probe records.
  - Converted ops: facing, profile rough/finish, chamfer, taper, multi-pass, boring. Grooving, parting, threading, form and drilling post as before.
- **The cache stays the nose centre.** The verifier, stock sim, gouge laws and CL goldens are unchanged. Orientation is not part of the op stamp, so editing it never stales an op.
- **Orientation fit, refused by name at post:** a corner tip reaches within 45° of its direction, an axis tip within 90°, and 9 fits anything.
  - Facing needs −Z and −X (2, 6, 7 fit), OD turning −X, boring +X.
  - A cut needing −X and +Z gives exactly [1, 5, 6], matching PathPilot's own refusal.
- **fanuc-lathe.cps:** the header states the control-point rule (G40). The tool note adds `ORIENTATION q` from a new commentary parameter `PARAM ToolOrientation`, documented in CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/630-nose-tip.md`.

## Golden diffs (Fanuc Lathe; r = 0.8, orientation 2)
- **`facing.nc`:** every changed line shifts X −1.6 (diameter) and Z −0.8. The last pass now posts the facing plane (Z14, was Z14.8).
  - Passes end at **X-1.6**: the nose centre still reaches the axis, so the control point stands r past centre. This is a normal facing overtravel, but a machine with a 0 X limit would need #631.
- **`profile_rough_finish.nc`:** shifts by X −1.6 / Z −0.8. The Ø12 flange posts **X12** (was X13.6), the shoulder Z2 (was Z2.8), and the Ø7 neck X7 (was X8.6). Three points differ by 0.001 from a pure shift because of 1 µm grid rounding.
- **Unchanged:** groove/part, axial drill, thread G76 and C-axis goldens. In `lathe_post.rs`, the facing assertion now expects `X-1.6 Z14` and `ORIENTATION 2`.

## How tested
- **`nose_tip` units (7):**
  - the OD finish posts the finished diameter, and a face posts Z0;
  - every orientation's offset;
  - a 30° taper is exact;
  - arcs keep their radius and move their centre;
  - the X-meridian case;
  - refusals;
  - orientation 9 is identity.
- **`orientation` units (3),** including PathPilot's [1, 5, 6].
- **App `lathe_nose_tip` (6):**
  - a Ø19.05 neck posts X19.05 and the shoulder Z0, while the cache stays nose-centre;
  - facing reaches the axis;
  - every fitting orientation equals cache + r·offset, and editing never stales the op;
  - mismatched orientations are refused;
  - ChangeTool undo/redo, and code 10 is refused;
  - a boring bar defaults to 3.
- **Round-trip and UI:** `project_roundtrip::a_lathe_orientation_round_trips_and_old_tools_take_the_default`, and the UI orientation row.
- **Gate:**
  - the non-thread turning and lathe suites, `lathe_post_g76`, conformance, golden_cl, posting, project_roundtrip and commands_undo;
  - the tool suites, c_axis_live, control_comp, wear_comp, program_entry, inverted_post and coolant_followups;
  - camcraft-post and camcraft-tools.
  - Clippy is clean on 5 crates.

## Follow-ups
- **Grooving and parting blades:** they post the centre of the blade's width, but a blade is touched off on a corner (LinuxCNC §4.2), so a width/2 Z offset is likely owed. Filed separately.
- **Refusal rule:** checking the leading direction would need insert lead angles, which the tool library doesn't model.
- **#626 (PathPilot lathe post):** consumes the converted stream once merged; its goldens need regenerating.
- **#639 (#629):** may hit small conflicts in test `Tool` literals.

Changelog: Lathe posts write the turning tool's control point for its orientation (LinuxCNC 1-9, editable per tool; default 2 for turning inserts, 3 for boring bars) instead of the nose-centre path: a Ø19.05 finish now posts X19.05 and a face at Z0 posts Z0; an orientation that cannot cut the operation is refused by name (#630)

- **xsTECH Pro:** the xsTECH Pro spec sheet (2026) and UM10859 (xsTECH Pro CE manual) §2.

## What changed
- **`assets/machines/tormach-24r.mch`:**
  - X 24.75 / Y 55.75 / Z 6.7 in;
  - 1.5 kW electrospindle, **10000-24000 rpm**;
  - 200 IPM on every axis;
  - ATC left unstated (optional, no station count given).
- **`assets/machines/tormach-xstech-pro.mch`:**
  - X 10.2 (with the standard tool changer);
  - **Y 7.9** (the CE manual) over the US sheet's 9.3, and Z 6.3 over the CE manual's 6.5. Where the documents disagree, the smaller travel is used, since it can only refuse a move, never let a bad one through;
  - 0.35 kW, max 20000 rpm with no minimum stated;
  - a 4-station ATC (T5 and up is refused);
  - **no feed ceiling stated**, because none is documented.
- **Both machines:**
  - rigid tapping false (not documented), so a tapping cycle is refused by name;
  - no coolant (none documented), so a Flood op is refused by name;
  - safe retract Z0, the Tormach convention.
- **Registration:** added to `MACHINES`. Both get the Tormach PathPilot mill post, as the Tormach mills do.

## How tested
- **New `tormach_routers` (4):**
  - the documents' figures;
  - the xsTECH Pro states no feed ceiling;

  - a **5000 rpm job is refused on the 24R** ("below the machine's 10000"), and the same job at 18000 posts.
- **Gate:** machine 32, machine_library, tormach_machines, tormach_safe_retract, tormach_post, posting and conformance pass. Clippy is clean.

A PathPilot Hub run of a profile on a router.

## The plain xsTECH Router (commit e1ff076d)
Tormach told the contributor that no separate manual was made for it (its documentation lives in the knowledge base). Its figures therefore come from Tormach's published spec sheet, product pages and knowledge base, each cited with its URL and retrieval date in the decision file.
- **Travel:** X 8.6 / Y 6.3 / Z 2.4 in. All sources agree.
- **Spindle:** 5000-15000 rpm, 0.08 kW, direct drive. The sources disagree (80-125 W, 3000/5000 to 15000/20000 rpm), so the narrowest window and the smallest motor are used: a refusal limit that is too narrow can only refuse a job, never pass a bad one. A 15-20k rpm job on a newer unit is refused by name, and the decision file says how to widen it.
- **Feed:** 120 IPM on every axis, as both feed and rapid. **Tool change:** manual ER11 collet, no ATC.
- **Rigid tapping and coolant:** not documented, so both are refused by name.
- **Left unstated:** a separate rapid rate, tool length and diameter limits, and 4th-axis figures.

**Tests:** `tormach_routers` 5 pass. The xsTECH spec row is new. The PathPilot posting test now covers all three routers (12000 rpm). `the_xstech_spindle_window_is_the_narrowest_stated` checks that 18000 and 4000 rpm are refused and 12000 passes. tormach_machines, machine, machine_library, posting, conformance, tormach_safe_retract and tormach_post pass, and clippy is clean.

title: feat(app,ui): part axes in the work plane by edge or two points; plane alignment picks faces only
body:
Two linked setup-page alignment changes on one branch. Both edit the same alignment picks, so they would conflict as separate PRs. The fork is synced at v0.15.0; branched with upstream/main merged.

## #557: set the part's X and Y in the work plane by an edge or two points (`bc2f5353`)
- **App** (`pick/axis.rs`, `turn_in_plane`):
  - **Pick:** an `AxisPick`, one straight edge or two vertices plus a flip, is read through the setup's current part alignment, so it composes after a face-to-plane lay.
  - **Turn:** the pick is projected onto the setup's XY, and the part turns about setup Z around its centre, so it stays on its spot of the table.
  - **Both axes:** the primary one (Y by default, or X) is laid exactly. The other is only checked: a parallel or left-handed pair is refused, never averaged.
  - **One axis:** the other follows right-handed (X = Y × Z).
  - **Precision:** quarter turns snap exactly.
- **Command:** the existing undoable `AlignPartToSetup` (new `turn_in_plane` / `check_turn` entries). The stock follows, linked setups follow, ops go stale and undo clears that. The same `part_alignment` field is used, so there is **no project-file change**.
- **Refused by name:** a face, a closed or curved edge, a single point, coincident points, an edge mixed with a point, a pick that isn't the part, a stale pick, a direction within 5° of the plane normal, a parallel or left-handed X/Y, nothing picked, a non-finite result, and "already holds the part that way".
- **UI:** a new "Axes in the plane - pick an edge or two points for +Y and/or +X" section on the setup page and the Setups overview.
  - Per axis: by Edge or by Two points, a Pick toggle, and Flip.
  - Then Primary, **Apply axes** (greyed with the reason; it shows the turn in degrees first) and Clear.
- **MCP:** `set_part_axes`.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/557-axis-by-edge.md`.

## #554: the setup page's plane alignment picks faces only (`7d641c8b`)
- **Plane row:** it now reads "Lay on a plane - pick a face" and arms Face mode, so a click beside an edge takes the face.
- **Removed:** the #330 two-edge plane mode. `pick::lay_on_plane` refuses an edge by name ("an edge cannot set a plane; pick a flat face (edges set an axis: Axes in the plane)").
- **Unchanged:** 3-2-1 alignment and operation-geometry edge picks.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/554-plane-pick-faces-only.md`.

## How tested
- **App `axis_align` (10):**
  - an edge at 30° → +Y, about the centre;
  - two points as X;
  - flip;
  - both axes, Y or X primary, plus the left-handed and parallel refusals;
  - a tilted pick projects cleanly;
  - near-normal and degenerate picks, a curved arc and a closed rim are refused;
  - undo and redo;
  - composes after a face lay;
  - stale, and undo clears it.
- **MCP:** `set_part_axes_turns_the_part_from_an_edge_or_two_points`.
- **UI:**
  - `setup_axis_tests` (3): edge → Apply → undo and redo, with a face refused; two points plus flip; an upright edge greys Apply with the reason.
  - New `plane_face_pick`: a real viewport click 4 px inside a face takes the face with the plane row armed, and the edge with an axis row armed.
  - `structural`: `setup_page_alignment_rows_structure`.
- **Updated:** `plane_align`, `plane_align_edges`, `winding_align` and `setup_plane_tests`, whose two-edge cases now expect the edge refusal (plus `every_edge_pick_is_refused_by_name`).
- **Gate:** setup_align, plane_align(_edges), winding_align, wcs_align, commands_undo, project_roundtrip, mcp, mcp_setup, mcp_pick, setup_relative and setup_carry pass, as do the ui boundary_picks and edge_loop_pick tests. ui lib passes 381 of 382; the one failure, the headless-GPU test, comes from the machine. Clippy is clean.

## Not exercised (draft)
A hands-on GUI check. The axis rows' clicks are fed to the draft in tests; the face/edge routing is pinned through a real viewport click.

**Deferred:**
- "Two points" takes model vertices only, not face centroids or typed coordinates.
- The work plane is always the setup's XY.

**Merge note:** #554 is a fix, but it rides with a feat, so this PR merges at the cut. If the fix is wanted sooner, `7d641c8b` can be split out.

Changelog: Setup alignment: set the part's +Y / +X in the work plane by picking a straight edge or two points (flip, Y or X primary), composed after a face-to-plane lay; one undoable step; MCP set_part_axes (#557)
Changelog: Setup page plane alignment picks faces only - a click beside an edge takes the face; the two-edge plane mode is removed and an edge is refused by name (#554)

Fixes #557
Fixes #554

title: feat(app,ui): locate the part in a fixture (or the fixture on the part) by face/point mates
body:
Locates the part in an imported fixture, or the fixture on the part, by face and point mates (#561, part of #339). Branched from the fork's main (synced at v0.15.0) with upstream/main merged.

## What changed
**Solver:** `fixture_locate.rs`, with the pure solve in `fixture_locate_solve.rs`. It takes one to three mates in the fixture's setup frame: face–face, point–point, point-on-face and face-on-point. It returns one rigid transform and never touches the WCS.
- **Order:** 3-2-1 fixturing. The first face mate opposes the normals by the shortest turn. The second turns the part about that normal. A third must already agree. Then each mate fixes the remaining free motion, in mate order.
- **Nudge:** after the mates, a turn about the first fixture normal, then an X/Y/Z shift.
- **Pick reader:** `pick/mate.rs` reuses `outward_normal` and `facets_centroid` (#187/#330).

**Commands** (`commands/locate.rs`):
- `LocatePart` moves the part through `MoveModel`, so the stock follows. In a turned setup (#326) it composes into `AlignPartToSetup` instead.
- `LocateFixture` moves the fixture by the inverse, through `MoveFixture`.
- `Locate` wraps both for the UI and MCP. Every locate is one undo step.

**Refused by name at creation:**
- **Bodies:** no fixture, the machine table, a model that isn't a fixture, no part, or a pick on the wrong body.
- **Picks:** an edge or curved face, a zero-area face, or two mates on the same point or face.
- **Solve:** faces that can't oppose, contradicting mates, zero mates or more than three, a non-finite nudge, or "nothing would move".

**Interpenetration warns rather than refuses.** A sampled inside test (the fixture mesh's ray law) names the part, the fixture and a point.

**UI:**
- **Fixtures page:** a **Locate part…** verb on each row.
- **Model page:** a locate row.
- **Form:** Move the part / Move the fixture, Offset X/Y/Z, Turn, **Apply locate** (greyed with the solve's reason) and Remove last.
- **Picks:** part first, then fixture, routed through the existing face and vertex picking.

**MCP:** a `locate_part` tool. `list_features` accepts a fixture.

## Choices that differ from the issue (decision file: `docs/decisions/561-locate-part-fixture.md`)
- **A moved fixture doesn't mark the setup's ops stale.** That keeps the existing rule that workholding never stales a toolpath. The collision check re-judges live instead, and a test pins it. Moving the part does mark them stale, and undo clears it.
- **Maintainer's call: in an unaligned setup the part moves through `MoveModel`.** That changes its document placement, so in a multi-setup document it also moves the part in the other setups, and their ops go stale and need regenerating. A translation-only setup alignment was avoided, because it would make the setup count as aligned and refuse every non-2D op. An alternative is to refuse a locate in an unaligned multi-setup document and point to aligning the setup first.
- **Deferred:** point-pair mates don't turn the part (only face mates orient it); there's no preview before Apply; per-setup part placement for unaligned multi-setup documents.

## How tested
- **App `fixture_locate` (11):**
  - a face mate makes the faces coplanar with opposed normals;
  - floor, jaw and stop give a full location;
  - the offset and turn are exact;
  - LocateFixture moves the fixture, not the part;
  - undo and redo;
  - point mates;
  - degenerate and conflicting picks are refused by name;
  - the interpenetration warning;
  - ops go stale and undo clears it;
  - a moved fixture is re-judged live while the path stays fresh;
  - the turned-setup case.
- **MCP:** `mcp_setup::locate_part_seats_the_part_on_the_fixture_by_feature_ids`.
- **UI:**
  - `locate_tests`: apply a locate from the Fixtures page, with undo and redo; the Model page moves the fixture to the part;
  - `fixture_rows`: the locate tools fit inside the pane on both pages;
  - `structural.rs`: no locate draft is armed by default.
- **Regressions:** `fixtures`, `fixture_ux`, `fixture_mesh`, `fixture_mesh_posed`, `setup_align`, `plane_align`, `commands_undo`, `project_roundtrip`, `mcp`, `mcp_setup` and `mcp_pick` all pass. ui lib passes 379 of 380; the failure is the headless-GPU test, which needs a graphics adapter this machine doesn't have. Clippy (app and ui, `-D warnings`) is clean.

## Not exercised (draft)
A GUI hands-on check (the picks in the viewport). That will be driven headless next.

Changelog: Locate the part in an imported fixture (or the fixture on the part) by face/point mates - floor, jaw, stop - with an offset and turn, from the Fixtures and Model pages and MCP locate_part (#561)

Fixes #561

title: feat(ui): Machines pane "Use for this setup" assigns the selected machine
body:
**Replaces #426** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #382** (Machines pane, browse + validate): this branch carries #382's commits plus a merge of current main. Merge #382 first; this PR's own diff is then the last two commits (`cb293f30`, `35cfa074`) plus the merge.

## What changed
- The Machines pane's detail view gets a **"Use for this setup"** button under the validation verdict. Clicking it queues `CommandKind::UseCatalogueMachine(MachineSource)`.
- It follows main's per-setup machine route (#343): `State::mount_catalogue` -> `route_machine(MachineVerb::Mount(..))`. If the active setup owns its machine, the selected machine replaces it (`SetSetupMachine`); otherwise the document's machine changes (`LoadMachine`). One undo step either way.
- Validation is re-run at assignment: `machine::library::read_for_assign` re-reads the built-in text or file, runs `validate_text`, and refuses with the first refusal, so a refused machine never mounts even if the command is queued directly. Shared by `LoadMachine::from_catalogue`, the new `SetSetupMachine::from_catalogue` and the UI route.
- The button is disabled with the reason shown under it and on hover: "fails validation - <first refusal> (and N more)" or "it is already this setup's machine" (reads `machine::of`, the active setup's effective machine).
- `MachineSource::mount_path()` mounts built-ins at `built-in: <name>`, the path the Setup pane's Library list already uses.
- Decision only (no code): the `machine_editor.rs` window becomes the pane's edit mode when the editing slice (#383) lands.

## Readings
Debug, M5 Mac. `scripts/gate.sh quick` (all camcraft-app + camcraft-ui suites): 1734 passed, 4 failed - all known reds on main (`setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` #415; GPU headless trio). Clippy `-D warnings` clean on app + ui.

## Pinning tests
- App `crates/app/tests/machine_assign.rs`: `assigning_a_catalogue_machine_does_undoes_and_redoes`, `a_refused_machine_cannot_be_assigned_and_says_why`, `a_setup_with_its_own_machine_takes_the_catalogue_machine`.
- UI lib `egui_app::tests::machines_pane`: `use_for_this_setup_assigns_the_selected_machine_and_undo_restores_it`, `a_refused_machine_cannot_be_assigned_and_names_why`, `use_for_this_setup_replaces_an_own_machine_and_leaves_the_document_alone`.

## Not exercised
No hand GUI run yet (**draft until the GUI check**); Ctrl+Y redo only at app level; disabled-hover text not asserted. Posted G-code unchanged (machines mount through the existing commands).

Decisions: `docs/decisions/384-machines-use-for-setup.md`.

Changelog: The Machines pane's "Use for this setup" assigns the selected machine to the active setup (its own machine or the document's), undoable; a machine that fails validation can't be assigned and says why

Fixes #384

title: feat(ui): preview the incoming stock in the viewport on the setup page
body:
**Replaces #429** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

## What changed
While a setup's settings page is open and its stock source is "What <previous setup> leaves behind", the viewport draws the incoming body as a translucent **teal** sheet, in the active setup's frame, distinct from the setup's own Stock node.

- App: new `setup_stock_view::incoming_shape(world, setup)` calls `stock_sim::incoming_body` once and returns the box/volume plus `body.display().surface(&[])` as triangles mapped into the viewport's frame (`A_active * inverse(A_setup)`; identity when the setup is active). An empty body or sheet is an error naming the setup; a bad index is skipped, never a panic.
- UI: `incoming_view::IncomingView` caches it keyed by (setup, active setup, `doc_version`) - measured once per document version, never per frame - refreshed at the end of `drain_actions` and cleared the moment the page closes, another page opens, or the setup switches to its own stock. A failed measurement is logged once and draws nothing.
- Drawing: `collect_parts` adds a stock-type part with vertex class 4; `fs_stock` paints class 4 as teal rgb (0.12, 0.66, 0.74) at alpha 0.45 in the existing translucent stock pass.
- The page's incoming box/volume text reuses the viewport's measurement, so there is one program sim per version instead of two.
- Display only: no command, nothing undoable (ephemeral view state per AGENTS.md). No files #412 touches were edited (`stock_sim*.rs`, `operation/*`, `rest/*`).

## Readings
Debug, M5 Mac. `scripts/gate.sh quick` (camcraft-app + camcraft-ui suites): 1718 passed, 4 failed - all known reds on main (`setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` #415; GPU headless trio). Clippy `-D warnings` clean. The changed WGSL shader was validated offline with naga 30.0.1; the `gpu_render` tests skip here (no adapter in the sandbox).

## Pinning tests
- UI lib `egui_app::incoming_view_tests`: `the_incoming_stock_shows_while_the_carried_setups_page_is_open` (real properties pane via egui_kittest: one class-4 part with Setup2's page open, top at Z 16 where Setup1 faced to; measured once, three more frames measure nothing, a `doc_version` bump measures once more; Close removes it), `no_incoming_stock_for_own_stock_or_another_page`.
- App `crates/app/tests/setup_stock_view.rs`: `the_sheet_stands_in_the_active_setups_frame`, `the_first_setup_draws_its_own_block_and_an_unknown_setup_is_named`.

## Not exercised
No real-GPU render of the teal and no hand GUI run yet - **draft until the GUI check**. Known limit: the traced whole-program stock view replaces all stock-type parts, so the overlay hides with it. Posted G-code unchanged.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/406-incoming-stock-preview.md`.

Changelog: The setup page previews the incoming (carried) stock in the viewport as a translucent teal body while a setup that takes what the previous setup leaves behind is open

Fixes #406
